item.title: Does the Global Sea-Level Rise Have a Sinusoidal Variation
item.description: I analysed the Tidal Gauge results of 9 ports in the northern regions of the Atlantic Ocean and above up to the Arctic Ocean. The analysis was very simplistic but showed promise so now a more detailed analysis will be carried out using procedures and methods developed more recently.

item.title: Victor Davis Hanson proclaims the “end of climate change”
item.description: “The inconsistency of the global warming narrative, the self-interest in the people who promote it, and the logic that they have not presented, empirically, the evidence that would convince us that we have to radically transform our economies on the wishes of a few elites that do not have the evidence, but do have a lot of hypocrisy in the process.”

item.title: Why is My Energy Bill Even Higher?
item.description: It is encouraging that opposition parties have started to challenge the Net Zero orthodoxy. The Green Blob should be left in no doubt that the trolley bus has been diverted and it is coming for it. Time to get out of the way.

item.title: “Tax the Rich”: The Successor to Net Zero?
item.description: The fact that Roger Hallam wants to use coercive government to impose his ‘solutions’ on others is a bulls-eye refutation that he is more of a megalomaniac than a clear-eyed scholar. His fringe views should be rejected and his proclivity for violence condemned

item.title: Claim: Household Bills are Causing Mental Distress – but Recycling More can Help
item.description: If you are worried about green energy prices, apparently the solution is to recycle more.

item.title: Does the Global Sea-Level Rise Have a Sinusoidal Variation–Part 2
item.description: The overall conclusion is that the 29-year variation is to do with the work involving the linear fitting but there is a general variation of about 18 years in all the tidal graphs which shows up in the full satellite data.

item.title: Affordability Crisis: Gavin Newsom and the California Energy Disaster
item.description: The newest Democrat party line is “affordability,” but renewable energy in California shows how not to be affordable.

item.title: Solar Bankruptcy: Pine Gate Renewables (boom to bust continues)
item.description: “What about the triple-digit number of creditors who banked on a loser? What about taxpayers who funded around 30 percent of the solar investment? … Ben Catt is just another rent-seeker, a political crony, like Sunnova’s John Berger, benefitting at the expense of just about everyone else.”

item.title: BP Abandon Teesside Hydrogen Plant
item.description: It cannot work without massive subsidies and I suspect BP have seen the writing on the wall. With interest in Net Zero dwindling and the public beginning to wake up the realities, BP are worried they will be left with a white elephant.
